bug_semantics: In Traefik's Kubernetes CRD provider, configBuilder.nameAndService (pkg/provider/kubernetes/crd/kubernetes_http.go) is the service-resolver for IngressRoute/TraefikService backendRefs. After the BIC, names without '@' still DeepCopy, fill Namespace from the parent, and reject via isNamespaceAllowed(allowCrossNamespace, parentNs, service.Namespace). Names containing providerNamespaceSeparator ('@') skip that entire branch. The only remaining gate is isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed(crossProviderNamespaces, parentNs), which returns true when the allowlist is nil (the default). Sibling resolvers (Provider.resolveReference for middlewares/TLS options; makeServersTransportKey for HTTP ServersTransport) already reject strings.HasSuffix(name, '@'+providerName) when allowCrossNamespace is false; nameAndService never did. A tenant confined to namespace attacker can therefore set services: [{name: '<victim-ns>-<svc>@kubernetescrd', kind: TraefikService}]. fullServiceName then splitSvcNameProvider-s the suffix, takes the pName==providerName (kubernetescrd) arm, and returns provider.Normalize(fmt.Sprintf('%s-%s', service.Namespace, name)). Because Namespace was never filled, service.Namespace is empty, so Normalize strips the leading hyphen and yields the victim TraefikService id ('<victim-ns>-<svc>'). The attacker's Host() router is generated bound to that backend despite providers.kubernetesCRD.allowCrossNamespace defaulting to false (Go zero-value bool; no SetDefaults sets it true).
flaw_origin: The isolation hole was first written by 36a565a599986afa9e2636d1e3f008c807ee13ec ('Fix cross-provider ref check for Kubernetes CRD provider', 2026-05-07, PR traefik/traefik#13121). Parent 28604083a41b6d6e8c206d71e0bce464bff1edb7 always DeepCopied the LoadBalancerSpec, filled Namespace via namespaceOrParentNamespace, and applied isNamespaceAllowed unconditionally, then called isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed against service.Namespace. That combination blocked namespace-field cross-ns TraefikService refs and, for '@kubernetescrd' names, prefixed the parent namespace in fullServiceName so 'victim-backend@kubernetescrd' became 'parent-victim-backend' rather than the victim id. The BIC wrapped both the DeepCopy/namespace fill and isNamespaceAllowed inside if !strings.Contains(service.Name, providerNamespaceSeparator), and restricted the crossProviderNamespaces check to '@'-names against parentNamespace. That is the exact skip-@ control flow the advisory describes. The commit did not copy the sibling '!allowCrossNamespace && HasSuffix(@kubernetescrd)' rejection already present in resolveReference and makeServersTransportKey, so '@kubernetescrd' TraefikService refs became an allowCrossNamespace=false bypass. This is not a move/refactor of already-exploitable lines: git log -L :nameAndService first attributes the skip wrapping to this commit, and the parent tree still has the unconditional isNamespaceAllowed. TraefikService resolution itself dates to f30a52c2 (2019) and allowCrossNamespace to 7ba907f2 (2020, default-false since 3072354c in 2021), but those earlier forms did not skip the namespace check/fill for '@' names.

git log -L :nameAndService:pkg/provider/kubernetes/crd/kubernetes_http.go first attributes the skip wrapping to 36a565a599986afa9e2636d1e3f008c807ee13ec (2026-05-07, 'Fix cross-provider ref check for Kubernetes CRD provider'). Diff: replaces unconditional DeepCopy+namespaceOrParentNamespace+isNamespaceAllowed with if !strings.Contains(service.Name, providerNamespaceSeparator) { ... isNamespaceAllowed ... } and changes the following gate to if !isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed(c.crossProviderNamespaces, parentNamespace) && strings.Contains(service.Name, providerNamespaceSeparator).

Parent verification: git rev-parse 36a565a5^ = 28604083a41b6d6e8c206d71e0bce464bff1edb7 (exists). Parent nameAndService (kubernetes_http.go:417-426) always DeepCopies, fills Namespace, and calls isNamespaceAllowed before any '@' handling; the skip-if is absent at the parent tree. TraefikService still returns fullServiceName(...) on both sides; the BIC is the first-write of the bypass control flow, not a move of that return.

Exploit path at BIC: fullServiceName (kubernetes_http.go:458-476) for port 0 and pName==providerName returns provider.Normalize(fmt.Sprintf('%s-%s', service.Namespace, name)). With '@' names, Namespace is left empty, so Normalize('-victim-backend') == 'victim-backend' (FieldsFunc drops the leading delimiter). isCrossProviderNamespaceAllowed (kubernetes.go:1230-1233) returns true when allowList==nil.

Sibling guards already present at the BIC and missing from nameAndService: Provider.resolveReference kubernetes.go:437-441 rejects !AllowCrossNamespace && HasSuffix(@kubernetescrd); makeServersTransportKey kubernetes_http.go:296-301 has the same HasSuffix rejection. The security fix copies that guard into nameAndService.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-71325 is a published GitHub CNA record matching GHSA-62fc-8686-hfmq; neither is withdrawn/rejected, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The sink is nameAndService's handling of kind=TraefikService backendRefs whose Name contains '@kubernetescrd'. Isolation allowCrossNamespace=false is on by default. The complete lifecycle is: (1) 2019 f30a52c2 introduced TraefikService + '@' provider names and fullServiceName's kubernetescrd prefixing; (2) 2020-21 7ba907f2/3072354c added allowCrossNamespace default-false and applied isNamespaceAllowed to the Namespace field in nameAndService; (3) sibling resolvers later gained an extra HasSuffix(@kubernetescrd) rejection because the Namespace field cannot see a namespace encoded in 'ns-name@kubernetescrd'; (4) 28604083 added CrossProviderNamespaces but still ran isNamespaceAllowed unconditionally; (5) 36a565a5 skipped that check/fill for every '@' name so genuine cross-provider refs (name@file) would work, and omitted the sibling @kubernetescrd rejection — first opening the bypass; (6) 65ebf4b added the missing rejection, shipped as v2.11.54 / v3.6.25 / v3.7.10. BIC choice: git log -L and the parent-tree diff identify 36a565a5 as the smallest product-history commit that first wrote the skip wrapping; parent 28604083 is present and still has unconditional isNamespaceAllowed, so introducer_parent_absent=false. GitHub PR #13121 is a 1-commit squash/rebase (member b0017e44, same tree and parent, same human author); decomposed_shas records that member. The BIC is not a move, backport, or multi-commit squash aggregate. Tag check: 36a565a5 is in the affected v2.11.53 / v3.6.24 / v3.7.9 tags and not in the patched tags until 65ebf4b lands (v2.11.54 / v3.6.25 / v3.7.10). GHSA's line-wide lower bounds (all v2.11, all v3.0+, all v3.7.0+) overstate introduction; the first-write of the exploitable skip is this May 2026 commit.
